title: Island cell reads filter to the granted feature
action: PBI p-9c48a67c read-side residue: .bee/cells/** is git-tracked, so a fresh granted worktree's island store legitimately holds every other feature's cell files on disk (ips-1 forbade pruning tracked files); those foreign cells then pollute island READS — status counts, cells list/ready output, claim-next scans and open-work derivations show another feature's cells as local work. Fix: at the shared cell-enumeration layer (find the one read path the consumers share — read.rs's listing functions are the hypothesis; if several enumerators exist, filter at the lowest shared seam, never per-consumer copies), when the resolved store root is a GRANTED worktree island (the grant identity is resolvable — see how registry.rs/roots resolve the granted feature for a worktree root), a cell file whose feature field names a DIFFERENT feature is skipped from enumeration. Tracked foreign files stay on disk untouched. The MAIN checkout's reads are byte-identical (no grant = no filter). Archived cells: same rule. TDD red-first: island fixture holding cells of features A (granted) and B -> list/ready/status counts show only A (red today); main-store fixture with several features shows all (pin byte-identical); claim-next in the island never offers B's cell.

truths: an island's cell reads show only the granted feature's cells
the filter lives at one shared seam, not per-consumer copies

artifacts.substantive: granted-feature read filter plus tests (or the real shared seam, named in the trace)

trace.outcome: island reads scope to the granted feature at both enumerators (cells/read.rs list_cells, status_full list+archive door); main reads pinned byte-identical; 9 new tests red-first
deviations: two enumerators exist (cells/read.rs and status_full/cells.rs), filtered at each lowest seam reusing read_worktree_feature; cells list/ready/claim-next CLI still refuse-delegate for granted worktrees at root resolution - widening those doors is a separate ask
